text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Mubarak meets the parliamentary committee of the ruling National Democratic Party, says: "All projects that have been implemented since I became responsible for the nation are aimed at transporting Egypt into the 21 century.

"We adjusted the housing law to oblige the government to obtain licences before it constructs institutions. State will spend five billion pounds on the next stage of developing the valley adjacent to the Nile valley. There are no differences or tensions between Egypt and the United States. The economic summit is being held to let the world know Egypt's capabilities"

- Mubarak congratulates Clinton on his re-election. Foreign Minister Moussa says "cooperation between Egypt and the U.S. will increase on the bilateral level. The U.S. is the main sponsor of peace in the region".
- Clinton is America's president for a second term after he won 379 votes compared to Dole's 148 votes. The Republicans control Congress and changes are expected in four ministries.
- Israel's foreign minister to visit today.
- Egypt sides with African leaders who want the world to send international troops to Zaire.

- Mubarak says "Egypt and the developing world is going through a hard time and we have to face the challenges. The government is doing its best for the people. The enemies of peace are trying to stop progress and Egypt is supporting the Palestinians and seeks to bring the points of view closer."
- The world welcomes Clinton's sweeping victory in the presidential elections.
- The Middle East manager of the International Monetary Fund says Egypt's economic reform programme is 100 percent Egyptian. Privatisation has helped reduce unemployment to 8.8 percent.
- Egypt to celebrate Pope Shenouda's ascension day tomorrow.
- IMF says Egypt's economic indicators make it the top spot for investment in North Africa.
- Mubarak says "We are building a new and modern state for the next century. We are facing many problems and the government is doing all it can to solve them."
- The heroin smugglers who tried to enter Egypt from the Red Sea were armed with American and Russian automatic rifles.
